title.en: Taiwan's Water Paradox: Too Much Rain, Not Enough Water

source.note: No workbook sheet exists for this SDG 6 mission; authored from scratch per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md.

narrative_brief: Taiwan gets 2.5 times the world's average rainfall but can use only a fifth of the world's average water per person. This talk traces that paradox from geography and typhoon dependency through the 2021 drought, reservoir sedimentation, diversification solutions, and the climate-driven squeeze between flood and drought risk.

stages.source_description: Part 1: Introduction (Slides 1-3: hook on the flood/drought contradiction, SDG 6 definition, Taiwan's rainfall-vs-usable-water paradox)

title.zh: 雨量豐沛卻缺乏可用水

stages.source_description: Part 2: Problem (Slides 4-6: steep terrain and short rivers, typhoon dependency and the 2021 no-typhoon drought, reservoir sedimentation)
stages.language_pattern: present progressive for trends / this causes ...

stages.source_description: Part 3: Achievements (Slides 7-9: the 2021 drought numbers and how Taiwan held on, desilting progress, supply diversification)
Part 4: Solutions (Slides 10-12: diversifying supply, replacing aging pipes, the hard case for pricing reform)

title.en: New pipes, not just new plants

stages.source_description: Part 5: Implications (Slides 13-16: climate change destabilising typhoons, flood risk rising alongside drought risk, the farm-vs-city trade-off, the cost to ordinary households) - one continuous tension: climate change is tightening the paradox, and the squeeze lands on real people

title.en: Climate change and the typhoon pattern
title.zh: 氣候變遷擾亂颱風規律
雨更多卻沒有解決問題

stages.source_description: Part 6: Call to action (Slides 17-20: summary of the paradox, reframing away from individual blame, what students can do, closing call)

title.en: Not a habit problem, a system problem
title.zh: 不是習慣問題而是系統問題

title.en: Engineer a system for whatever comes
title.zh: 打造能應對未來的系統
